home.heroSub: Prices, long-run averages and cycle measures for the largest crypto-assets, each with its method and its limits. Macro and global markets are planned.

methods.title: Methods
methods.intro: Every number on this site comes from one of these models. Each page states the method, its assumptions and its limits, and how it was checked.

about.title: About
about.whatBody: A research service for crypto and global markets: data from licensed sources, the published methods applied to it, and the limits of both. It offers information and education only.
about.sourcesBody: Crypto prices: Bitstamp's daily closes. Data is used only where the source's terms allow it, and each source is named beside the figures that use it.
about.tiersBody: The main figures are free. The full chart library and deeper analysis will be part of paid plans once accounts open. Plan rules are applied on our server: information outside your plan is never sent to your browser, and the same applies to e-mail.
about.correctionsBody: Sources are stored exactly as published, and every calculation is versioned. When a source corrects a figure, the correction is applied and the earlier value is kept on record.

footer.tagline: Information and education on crypto and global markets. Not investment advice.

learn.title: Learn the basics
learn.intro: Plain-language explanations of the terms used on this site.

movingAverage.name: Moving average
movingAverage.short: The average price over a fixed number of recent days or weeks, recomputed every day.
movingAverage.long: A 200-day average is the mean of the last 200 daily closes. It smooths out day-to-day moves, so it shows the longer direction of the price. An exponential average weights recent days more. Averages describe the past; they do not predict.

drawdown.name: Drawdown
drawdown.short: How far the price is below its highest close so far.
drawdown.long: A drawdown of −50% means the price is half its highest close to date. It returns to 0 only on a day the price sets a new high. Here the high is the highest close in the data, which starts in 2011 for bitcoin.

volatility.name: Realised volatility
volatility.short: How much the price has been moving, as a yearly percentage.
volatility.long: The standard deviation of daily price changes over the last 30 or 90 days, scaled to a year (√365, because crypto trades every day). 80% means typical yearly swings of that size. It measures the past, not risk to come.

halving.name: Halving
halving.short: The day the number of new bitcoins created with each block halves, every 210,000 blocks (about four years).
halving.long: Halvings so far: 28 November 2012, 9 July 2016, 11 May 2020 and 20 April 2024. The periods between them are often called epochs. Past prices around them are shown as history, not as a pattern that must repeat.

powerLaw.name: Power law
powerLaw.short: A straight-line trend on a chart whose both axes are logarithmic.
powerLaw.long: Here: log price against log of the days since bitcoin's first block (3 January 2009). The line summarises how fast the price has grown so far. It is a description of the past, not a value the price should have.

methodVersion.name: Method version
methodVersion.short: Every calculation has a version number.
methodVersion.long: When we change how something is calculated, the version changes and the earlier version stays on record, so a figure can always be traced to the method that produced it.

marketCap.name: Market capitalisation
marketCap.short: The value of all units of an asset at today's price.
marketCap.long: For a crypto-asset, the number of coins in circulation multiplied by the price; for a company, its shares in issue multiplied by the share price. It shows size as the market values it today, not what the asset is worth to anyone in particular.

logScale.name: Logarithmic scale
logScale.short: A chart axis where each step is the same percentage change, not the same amount.
logScale.long: On a log scale, a rise from $100 to $200 takes the same height as one from $10,000 to $20,000: both are a doubling. It makes long histories with very large moves readable.

mayer.name: Mayer multiple
mayer.short: The price divided by its 200-day average.
mayer.long: 1.5 means the price is 50% above its 200-day average; 0.8 means 20% below. It describes how far the price has moved from its recent average, nothing more.

feedback.title: Tell us what you think
feedback.intro: This service is new, and what you tell us decides what we build next. Your message goes to the two of us who run it; it is never shown on the site.

topics.data_error: A number looks wrong or out of date
topics.idea: An idea or a request for a feature

feedback.messageHelp: Between {min} and {max} characters. Please leave out your name, phone number and other personal details: we do not need them.
feedback.privacy: We keep your message and the page it is about. We do not keep your name, e-mail or network address; a scrambled form of the address is kept for seven days only, to stop floods of messages. Ask us and we will delete your message.
feedback.notAdvice: We cannot answer questions about what you personally should do with your money: this service gives information and education only.

thanks.title: Thank you
thanks.ok: Your feedback has been received. We read every message.
thanks.limited: You have sent a lot in the last hour, so this one was not stored. Please try again later.
thanks.invalid: Something was missing, so nothing was stored. Please choose a topic and write a few words.
thanks.unavailable: Feedback is not switched on yet on this copy of the site, so nothing was stored.

crypto.title: Crypto markets
crypto.intro: Global crypto-asset prices in US dollars, from Bitstamp's daily closes, with the history and long averages that describe them.
crypto.prototype: Prototype: the data licence for this section is pending. Until Bitstamp's data agreement is signed, these pages are for the owners' private preview only.
crypto.history: Price history starts where Bitstamp's does: 14 September 2011 for bitcoin, and later for every other asset. Earlier prices, including bitcoin's 2011 high, are not included.
crypto.utcDay: Each day is a UTC day (00:00 to 24:00 UTC); its price is the day's last trade on Bitstamp.
crypto.btcChart: Bitcoin's price and its 200-week average (weekly points, log scale)

cryptoAsset.drawdownChart: Fall from the highest close to date
cryptoAsset.bandChart: Price with the 20-week and 21-week averages, and the 200-week average
cryptoAsset.crossings: Days the Pi cycle lines crossed
cryptoAsset.crossingsNone: The lines have not crossed in this asset's Bitstamp history.
cryptoAsset.crossingsNote: Listed as facts about past data. The settings of these lines were chosen by their author to fit past highs and lows, so their record is not a test, and it says nothing about what happens next.
cryptoAsset.cycleTable: Halvings, cycle peaks and cycle lows
cryptoAsset.cycleTableNote: A cycle's peak and low are the two ends of the largest fall between two halvings, on Bitstamp closes. Provisional: the epoch has not ended, so the date can still move.
cryptoAsset.since: Change since, to the latest close
cryptoAsset.monthlyNote: Each completed month's last close against the previous month's. This month so far: {pct}.
cryptoAsset.trendNote: Two straight lines through bitcoin's whole Bitstamp history on log-log axes, re-fitted every day on the data to that day, with bands one and two standard deviations either side. They summarise past growth; they are not a value the price should have, and not a forecast.
cryptoAsset.positionNote: 0 at the lower outer band, 1 at the upper
cryptoAsset.fit_log_regression_note: every stretch of log-time weighted equally
cryptoAsset.trendBtcOnly: The trend bands are computed for bitcoin only.
